notes: GetDataObject: stamp check against data_stamps_ (+0x550), then id lookup in data_objects_ and data_pending_ (under +0x60). The handle write-back uses SetTimeStamp with the slot as the second word, which the original call does not show.
GetUserData: -1 without an object. Returns the low 32 bits of the pointer-sized user word, as the int return of the header allows.
SetUserData: read access, then DataObj::SetUserData when the object exists.
ReleaseDatasource(DataHandle): NeedToDie, then queued once on data_queue_ (queued_ flag at +0x4c).
IncreaseDataObjectRefCount: calls Handlable::Retain (object vtable slot +0x08, checked against vtables-001.json).
Initialize: CreateDriver is not ported, so the driver stays null. FileSystemInterface::GetInstance has no effect and is not called.

C1 constructor: master and group fades, priority bank (8), default 3D parameters. Not reproduced: container id counters start at 1 in the original (0 in the port), the reserve() calls, the +0x43c list head and the +0x598 buffer.
C2 constructor: same body as C1, with the same missing parts.
ReleaseDatasource(group id): NeedToDie and queue for every data object whose group bits match, in data_objects_ and data_pending_.
ReleaseDatasource(DataObj*): stamp slot bump, detach and kill each emitter (DetachEmitterObject not reconstructed), destroy decoder, stream and object. Emitters are taken from a copy, last first.
_ReleaseAllDatasource: releases each object of data_objects_ and data_pending_, then drops the entries with Detach (Clear would delete them twice).
DetachDataObject: data_objects_ first, then data_pending_ under the data write access.
DecreaseDataObjectRefCount: calls Handlable::Release (object vtable slot +0x0c), then queues the object for release.
GetAllDataSources: fills out from data_objects_ then data_pending_, returns the count (header changed from void to int).
LoadDataSourceAsync: stream and decoder from the factory tables; object left in the loading state (3) with its flags, added to data_pending_ and queued for the update loop.

LoadDataSource: probes a cursor and requires channels > 0. Track parameters come from decoder GetParam, not from the cursor block at +4..+0x10, which the port cursor does not have. Failed attempts destroy the stream and decoder.
ConvertToRamBufferSource: reads the whole stream into a buffer, then LoadDataSource with the memory-buffer stream (type 0) and the decoder type and parameter block.

ConvertToRawSource: decodes with a decoder cursor into channels * length * bytes-per-sample bytes, then LoadDataSource with raw decoder type 0. Size and parameters come from GetParam (see LoadDataSource). The read access is released on the no-cursor path; the Hex-Rays body shows no release there.

D1 destructor: _ReleaseAllDatasource, VoxNativeSubDecoder::Clean, delete priority bank and driver, clear s_voxEngineInternal. Not reproduced: FileSystemInterface::DestroyInstance (not ported) and the +0x598 buffer (owner not identified).
D0 deleting destructor: compiler-generated wrapper of the D1 above; partial for the same reasons.
D2 destructor: same body as D1, with the same missing parts.
